chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no problem with the fish which the Magian hunts.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is fish caught by Magians permissible to eat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that fish caught by Magians (Majusi) is permissible (halal) for consumption, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the primary source of fish purity is the water itself rather than the catcher's specific religious status. It underscores the distinction between the general permissibility of aquatic life and the specific rulings on land animals, emphasizing that the Magian's act of fishing renders the catch valid for Shia Muslims.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is no problem with the fish which the Magians hunted (fished)’.
en.sarwar: 13. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
It is not unlawful to use for food the fish which is caught by Zoroastrians.’”
